title: Neonatal HIE & Therapeutic Hypothermia
sources: Critical Vector — Neonatology Pocket Guide: HIE & Therapeutic Hypothermia
Sarnat HB, Sarnat MS. Arch Neurol 1976;33:696-705
NICHD (Shankaran S et al. NEJM 2005), TOBY (Azzopardi DV et al. NEJM 2009), CoolCap (Gluckman PD et al. Lancet 2005)

changelog.change: Initial entry — Sarnat staging, therapeutic-hypothermia eligibility and method, the pooled trial outcome, and the multiorgan involvement to expect.

purpose: In moderate-to-severe HIE, therapeutic hypothermia started within 6 hours of birth reduces death or major neurodevelopmental disability — it reduces, but does not eliminate, the risk. Recognise it early, stage it on the Sarnat exam, and start cooling on time.

body.text: Sarnat staging (bedside exam at 30–60 min → a few hours of life)
Modified Sarnat scoring systems (NICHD, SIBEN) are used for trial eligibility; the original 3-stage framework remains the bedside standard. Only Stage II or III meets cooling criteria.
Therapeutic hypothermia — eligibility (combination required; varies by protocol)

items: Evidence of perinatal hypoxia-ischaemia: Apgar ≤ 5 at 10 min, OR ongoing resuscitation / PPV at 10 min, OR a cord or early neonatal pH / base deficit meeting the protocol's cutoff.
Moderate or severe encephalopathy (Sarnat II or III) on an exam done in the first hours of life.
Cooling INITIATED within 6 hours of birth.

body.text: Method: selective head cooling OR whole-body cooling to a core temperature of 33.5–34.5 °C for 72 hours, then controlled slow rewarming (typically over 6–12 h). Eligibility criteria (required pH / base-excess cutoffs, the exact encephalopathy score) vary meaningfully between regional protocols — use YOUR institution's protocol for patient selection, not a single fixed number. Passive cooling can start during transport while the receiving centre is contacted.

Pooled RCT outcome (CoolCap, NICHD, TOBY): therapeutic hypothermia reduces the combined outcome of death or major neurodevelopmental disability in moderate-severe HIE — but a substantial proportion of treated infants still have an adverse outcome.

rows: Transient myocardial dysfunction, cardiogenic shock, tricuspid regurgitation
Meconium aspiration, persistent pulmonary hypertension of the newborn (PPHN)
Necrotising enterocolitis risk — delay / minimise enteral feeds

buildNote: Tier 1. HIE is the commonest cause of neonatal seizures — cross-linked. aEEG monitoring during cooling is standard where available.  Related: nrp-algorithm, neonatal-seizures, neonatal-jaundice, hyperosmolar-therapy.
